name: Transfer printing
summary: A design is engraved on a copper plate, printed on thin paper in a ceramic ink and moved from the paper to the glazed or biscuit piece.
how: Engrave the design on a copper plate.
Print it on thin tissue paper in ceramic ink.
Press the wet tissue on the piece and rub it down.
Wash the paper away and fire the piece to fix the ink.

origin.note: John Sadler and Guy Green of Liverpool print tiles and Worcester soon prints porcelain.

adoptions.via: Soft-paste tea ware takes printed landscapes and flower designs in black and blue.
